reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Strong evidence - avelumab achieved therapeutic serum concentrations (172-300 μg/mL), indicating adequate drug exposure and likely PD-L1 binding. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: Limited evidence - PD-L1 expression was measured but changes not clearly reported; anti-drug antibodies in 15/67 patients suggests immune system engagement but may compromise efficacy. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: Mixed results - ORR ranged from 33.3% to 53.8% across different dose/combination arms, which appears clinically meaningful for advanced NSCLC/urothelial cancer, but no statistical significance testing reported and no comparator arm. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: 28/41 patients were PD-L1 positive at baseline, suggesting enriched population, but specific response rates by PD-L1 status not clearly reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Single-arm design prevents definitive efficacy assessment; significant toxicity (grade 3+ neutropenia in 51% of main cohort) may have limited optimal dosing; immunogenicity in 22% of patients could reduce efficacy.

failure_modes.evidence: No statistical significance testing, no comparator arm, and limited reporting of biomarker-response relationships prevent definitive efficacy assessment
Grade 3+ neutropenia in 21/41 patients (51%) and serious cardiac events may have prevented optimal dosing and treatment duration

edges_to_update.reasoning: Therapeutic serum concentrations achieved, confirming target engagement
Anti-drug antibodies in 22% of patients may compromise sustained immune checkpoint blockade
ORR of 33-54% suggests biological activity, though without comparator cannot assess magnitude

review_reason: Single-arm design with no statistical testing makes efficacy assessment ambiguous; significant toxicity and immunogenicity complicate interpretation of mechanism validation
